description: Task 3.1 CLI Tool. Turn the placeholder xplainit-cli crate into a real clap-based binary with subcommands `run`, `explain`, `analyze`, and `report`, reusing existing xplainit-core types (EventStore, ErrorExplainer, FormatterFactory/HtmlFormatter/JsonFormatter). This is the first Phase 3 feature and also serves as environment baseline confirmation (the workspace builds/tests green today; verify before starting).
steps: Confirm baseline: from repo root run `cargo build --release`, `cargo test`, and `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`; all must be green before changing anything.

Re-enable the CLI crate: in the root Cargo.toml [workspace] members list, uncomment/add "xplainit-cli" (it is currently commented out as '# "xplainit-cli", # Not yet implemented'). Confirm xplainit-cli/Cargo.toml already depends on xplainit-core, clap 4 (derive+cargo), anyhow, colored, serde_json, tokio.
Do NOT add new external crates that are not already in Cargo.lock (network is repository-access-only). clap/serde_json/colored/anyhow/tokio are already available.

Replace xplainit-cli/src/main.rs with a real clap derive CLI. Define a `Cli` with `#[command(subcommand)]` and a `Commands` enum with these subcommands matching the plan sketch: `run { file: String }`, `explain { target: String }` (accepts the `file::function` form), `analyze { log: String }`, `report { trace: String, #[arg(long, default_value="text")] format: String }`. Consider splitting handlers into small modules under xplainit-cli/src/ (e.g. commands/run.rs, explain.rs, analyze.rs, report.rs) with main.rs wiring them via clap.

Implement `analyze <log.json>`: read the JSON file, deserialize into Vec<ExecutionEvent> (ExecutionEvent already derives Serialize/Deserialize), run xplainit_core::ErrorExplainer over the events, and print the resulting ErrorAnalysis in a human-readable, colored form. Handle file-not-found and malformed-JSON with clear anyhow errors (non-zero exit).

Implement `report <trace.json> --format <text|json|html|markdown>`: read the JSON trace into Vec<ExecutionEvent>, use xplainit_core::FormatterFactory / the formatter matching the requested format (map the string to OutputFormat) to render the events, and print to stdout. Reuse existing formatters; do not reimplement HTML.

Implement `explain <file::function>`: parse the `path::function` argument (split on the last `::`). Since the CLI cannot instrument a live process in-sandbox, use xplainit-core AST support (ast.rs AstParser) if feasible to describe the function, otherwise produce a clear, honest explanation-scaffold message and, when a matching trace JSON is available, filter/explain events for that function using ExplanationGenerator. Document in code comments exactly what is and is not wired to a live runtime.

Implement `run <file>`: detect language by extension. Full live tracing of an arbitrary external program requires the language runtime hooks and is not wired end-to-end from the CLI in-sandbox; implement what is genuinely runnable (e.g. for a JSON trace or a supported path) and for the not-yet-wired case emit a clear, explicit message about what is required, rather than pretending it traced. Do not print success it did not achieve.

Add unit/integration tests in xplainit-cli (e.g. tests/ or #[cfg(test)] mod): write a small sample trace JSON fixture (a couple of ExecutionEvent values incl. one error event) into a temp file and assert that `analyze` and `report --format json/html` produce expected non-empty, correct output. Use assert_cmd only if it is already in Cargo.lock; otherwise call the command handler functions directly and/or drive the binary via std::process::Command against the built binary.
Keep clippy clean (-D warnings) and run cargo fmt.
acceptance_criteria: Root Cargo.toml [workspace] members includes xplainit-cli and `cargo build --release` builds the `xplainit` binary.
`xplainit --help` lists run, explain, analyze, report subcommands.
`xplainit report --format json <trace.json>` and `--format html <trace.json>` emit valid formatted output produced via xplainit-core formatters (not hand-rolled in the CLI).
`xplainit analyze <log.json>` reads a JSON event log and prints ErrorExplainer analysis for error events.
New tests exercise at least the analyze and report paths and would fail if those handlers were reverted to the placeholder.
cargo test, cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings, and cargo fmt --all -- --check all pass for the whole workspace.
verification: Build then run: ./target/release/xplainit --help; ./target/release/xplainit report --format json <sample-trace.json>; ./target/release/xplainit analyze <sample-log.json> and confirm real, non-empty output.
findings: Implemented the xplainit CLI in xplainit-cli. Re-enabled the crate in the root Cargo.toml [workspace] members. Replaced the placeholder src/main.rs with a clap derive CLI (Cli + Commands enum) and split handlers into src/commands/{mod,analyze,report,explain,run}.rs. No new external crates were added; Cargo.lock is unchanged (clap 4.6.7, serde_json, colored, anyhow, tokio were already present). WHAT WORKS END-TO-END: `analyze <log.json>` loads a Vec<ExecutionEvent> and prints colored ErrorExplainer/ErrorAnalysis output for every error event; `report <trace.json> --format text|json|html|markdown` renders via xplainit-core FormatterFactory (JSON path returns the formatter's complete array and deliberately skips the header/footer wrappers so output stays a single valid JSON array; text/html/markdown use header+body+footer); `explain <file::function>` splits on the LAST '::', statically describes the function via the core AstParser (Tree-sitter) when the source file exists, and, when --trace is supplied, filters events for that function and explains them with ExplanationGenerator; `run <file>` renders a pre-captured .json trace (genuinely working) and for source files prints an explicit not-wired message naming the required language binding. HONESTY / NOT WIRED: live instrumentation of an external program from the CLI (run of source, and attach-and-explain of a live process) is NOT wired - those paths emit an explicit actionable message instead of faking success; documented in module/doc comments. TESTS: 6 unit tests (analyze_events, report::render across json/html/markdown/error) + 6 integration tests in tests/cli.rs driving the built binary via std::process::Command (assert_cmd is NOT in Cargo.lock; tempfile is but I used std::env::temp_dir per-test dirs). Test fixture events are built by deserializing JSON to avoid adding uuid/chrono as direct CLI deps. All 12 pass and would fail if handlers reverted to the placeholder. VERIFICATION: `cargo build --release`, `cargo test` (whole workspace, 12 new + all prior green), and `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` all PASS. PRE-EXISTING ISSUE (not caused by this change, verified with git stash at HEAD): `cargo fmt --all -- --check` fails repo-wide (32 files across every crate, e.g. xplainit-core/src/*, xplainit-python/src/tracer.rs) because the sandbox rustfmt 1.8.0 / rustc 1.92.0 reformats the older codebase differently than it was originally formatted. My new xplainit-cli files ARE fmt-clean (verified with `cargo fmt -p xplainit-cli -- --check`). I intentionally did NOT reformat the 32 unrelated pre-existing files to avoid a massive out-of-scope diff; a separate repo-wide `cargo fmt --all` pass is recommended to green the fmt gate.
